title: Frugal Assembler: cost-first batching advisor with KV-cache awareness
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Build a production-safe recommendation engine that proposes batching and caching configurations optimized for per-customer token economics while respecting latency SLOs and KV-cache effectiveness. The advisor ingests workload fingerprints (seq length distribution, caller QPS, tail latency, prefix reuse), runs a lightweight simulation/estimation, and outputs tuned parameters (microbatch size, pack-window, cache TTL, reuse thresholds, packing strategies) with a staged apply/rollback plan.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor generates actionable config suggestions for ≥90% of profiled workloads in the pilot orgs
Simulated cost delta estimate within ±10% of measured cost after 72-hour shadow run
Automated safe-apply mechanism that can abort and rollback within N seconds when golden signals regress
End-to-end tests + canary pipeline in CI that prevents rollout if spike in 95th/99th latency metrics is detected
proposal: Run continuous lightweight profilers in runtime nodes to produce 1h/24h fingerprints (histograms of seq lengths, joint distribution of model+route, prefix-reuse ratios)

Combine heuristics with a small bandit-style optimizer: seed from heuristic rules (e.g., high prefix reuse -> larger pack-window), then explore +/- options during shadow applies to refine parameters per workload cluster
KV-cache-awareness: compute expected cache hit delta for candidate pack sizes and prefer configs that improve cache effectiveness even if raw batching gain is modest
Safety-first rollouts: shadow apply → canary (5% traffic) → ramp with automatic rollback triggers based on latency, error rate, and tail KPIs
Provide per-customer narrative and estimated cost/latency impact in the Console and expose an API to accept/decline suggestions
implementation_notes: Profiler output format: compressed histogram + small fingerprint key (model, route, median len, p95 len, reuse_score)
Simulation engine: deterministic cost model using token counts, kernel utilization baseline, and cache hit model. Implement as a Go service co-located with runtime for fast feedback loops
Use existing rollout infra (rollouts API) but extend it with a fast rollback circuit that cancels in-flight config patches and restores previous KV cache TTLs/pack-windows
Data retention: keep profilers for 30 days; maintain experiment metadata for 90 days for offline analysis
Instrument golden signals (p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, successful cache hit rate) and emit to metrics + trace logs for per-suggestion audits
testing_plan: Unit tests for cost model using recorded traces (three distinct workload archetypes)
Integration test that runs 24h shadow profile, applies recommended config to shadow nodes, and compares cost estimate vs measured tokens and latency
Chaos test that induces sudden QPS spikes to validate rollback thresholds (simulate 2x QPS for 10 minutes)
CI gating: PRs must include a small simulator run and smoke asserts for golden metrics
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dev org only (2 teams) — collect fingerprints and validate offline estimates
Phase 1: shadow applies across 10% of traffic in non-production staging clusters
Phase 2: canary apply (5% production traffic) with 30-minute observation window and automatic rollback triggers
Phase 3: gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with monitoring and manual guardrails for enterprise tenants
Fallback: immediate revert + incident ticket if auto-rollback fails to restore baseline within 10 minutes
risks: Over-aggressive packing may increase tail latency for long-context traffic — mitigated by per-route limits and simulation checks
Incorrect cache-effect model could suggest configs that reduce effective hit-rate — mitigate by conservative estimates and validation against real cache metrics
Cross-tenant variability: a global heuristic may hurt niche workloads — solution: per-customer profiles and opt-out flag
Stateful rollback complexity: changing pack-window interacts with in-flight KV caches; ensure atomic swap semantics and a short quiesce window
